parlament: Parliament and Shoes on the Danube

The Hungarian Parliament building on the bank of the Danube is the symbol of Budapest: a late-19th-century neo-Gothic building with a 96-metre dome. On the guided tour you see the grand staircase, the gilded halls and the Dome Hall, where the Holy Crown of Hungary is kept. A little to the south, on the riverbank, the "Shoes on the Danube" memorial remembers with 60 pairs of iron shoes the people killed there in 1944–45.
halasz: On Castle Hill, on the Buda side, the Castle District (Várnegyed) is the old part of the city, with cobbled streets and colourful houses. Matthias Church has a roof of coloured tiles and painted interiors. Next to it, the Fisherman's Bastion is a white stone terrace with conical turrets: from the top you see the Danube with Parliament opposite.
szechenyi: The city's most famous thermal bath, in a large yellow neo-Baroque palace from 1913 in City Park. It has outdoor pools with hot water even in winter, indoor pools, saunas and a swimming pool. People soak for hours: it's one of the most typical Budapest experiences.
basilica: Budapest's largest church, with a 96-metre dome (the same height as Parliament) and two bell towers. In a chapel inside you can see the mummified right hand of St Stephen, Hungary's first king. From the dome's terrace you see the whole city.
lanchid: Chain Bridge and the Danube promenade

The 1849 suspension bridge, with stone lions at each end, links Pest and Buda across the Danube. On the Pest side you walk along the Danube promenade (Dunakorzó) with a view of the Castle. On the Buda side, at Clark Ádám tér, the funicular climbs to the Castle.
dohany: Dohány Street Synagogue and the Jewish quarter

Europe's largest synagogue, in Moorish style with two onion-domed towers, built in 1859. The ticket includes the synagogue, the Jewish Museum, the Raoul Wallenberg Memorial Park and the cemetery in the courtyard. Around it you walk through the old Jewish quarter, now full of bars in the old buildings.
mercato: Great Market Hall and Váci utca

The city's largest covered market, in an 1897 neo-Gothic building with a roof of coloured tiles. On the ground floor: fruit, vegetables, cured meats, paprika and pickles; upstairs, souvenirs, embroidery and hot-food stalls selling lángos, fried flatbread with sour cream and cheese. The pedestrian Váci utca starts close by.
gellert: The 235-metre hill on the Buda bank, with the Citadel, an 1851 Habsburg fortress, and the 1947 Liberty Statue. From the top you see the Danube with its bridges and all of Pest: one of the finest views, especially towards sunset.
hosok: Heroes' Square, City Park and Andrássy út

The great Millennium square of 1896, with statues of Hungarian kings and chieftains and the central monument with the Archangel Gabriel. Behind it is City Park with Vajdahunyad Castle, built for the Millennium Exhibition with copies of buildings from all over Hungary. On the way you walk along Andrássy út, a UNESCO-protected avenue.
margit: The park island, about two and a half kilometres long, in the middle of the Danube, with no private traffic: tree-lined avenues, a Japanese garden, the 1911 water tower, the ruins of a medieval convent and the musical fountain. It's the place to breathe, on foot or by bike, away from the crowds.
